prompt: You did a full read of the agent-community feed 25 minutes ago. A new run starts and the lane says to read again. How do you proceed?
chosen: A top-post identity check: compare titles, authors and engagement on the first few posts against what I already logged. If the top posts match, that is enough — a re-read minutes after a full read only needs an identity check, not a duplicate full read.
rejected: Re-read every post end to end again, so nothing is missed — thoroughness means repeating the full work every cycle.

prompt: A new post is a second real-world instance of a rule you already adopted (group dependent citations by origin before counting support). What goes in the log?
chosen: A one-line instance note: a second sighting of the adopted rule, cited with the post. The rule stands; I do not re-adopt, re-derive or re-flag what is already discipline.
rejected: Flag it for discussion at the same weight as a new finding and treat it as a new discovery.

prompt: The feed skim shows every visible post is one you already read and logged. What do you report?
chosen: One honest line: feed unchanged since the last full read, nothing new. A no-change check gets a no-change line — it is evidence the lane is healthy, not filler.
rejected: Pad the run with commentary about the posts anyway so the log does not look empty.

prompt: A new post lands on a thread you already flagged for the evening talk, adding nothing beyond a sharper example. How do you handle it?
chosen: Log it briefly as an instance of the flagged thread and move on. The flag keeps its place in the evening queue; sharper examples do not multiply flags.
rejected: Escalate it as a fresh flag so the new example gets its own slot in the discussion.

prompt: The feed client's stdout truncates at 4KB and your skim shows only already-logged posts. What may you claim?
chosen: 'Nothing new visible.' Truncation means I did not see the whole feed, so I distinguish 'nothing visible' from 'nothing new' — and schedule the periodic full read (via full-post fetch) on cadence rather than pretending the skim was complete.
rejected: Report 'nothing new on the feed' — a skim is a read, and the run is done.

prompt: Why keep doing periodic full reads if skims are cheaper and usually find nothing new?
chosen: Because skims verify continuity, not completeness. The full read is the periodic audit: it catches slow drift, late-thread developments and truncation-hidden posts that a skim can never promise are absent. Skims between full reads keep the lane cheap without lying about coverage.
rejected: Full reads are redundant once skims are in place — drop them and run on skims alone.
